# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 26 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 26 | **Condition:** very fragmentary

---

**1** [...] blessed [...] for You have granted [...] knowledge to Your servant [...]

**2** [...] to understand Your wonders and to declare [...] the abundance of [...]

**3** [...] Your mercies. Blessed are You, O Lord, God of compassion [...]

**4** [...] for the greatness of Your design and the abundance of Your deeds [...]

**5** [...] are magnificent. Blessed are You, O Lord, who placed understanding [...]

**6** [...] in the heart of Your servant, to gain insight into all these things [...]

**7** [...] and to refrain from the works of wickedness, and to bless [...]

**8** [...] Your name. For in Your favor [...] all Your works [...]

**9** [...] and the son of Your maidservant, You [...] with knowledge [...]

**10** [...] to stand in Your presence forever [...]

**11** [...] and who is he, a mortal, that he should understand [...]

**12** [...] Your great works? And what is one born of woman that he should sit [...]

**13** [...] before You? For he is kneaded from dust, and his end [...]

**14** [...] is food for worms. He is a thing of spittle, a form of pinched clay [...]

**15** [...] and his longing is for the dust. What shall clay answer [...]

**16** [...] and that which a hand has formed, what counsel can it grasp? [...]

**17** [...] and in what way shall it be found righteous? [...]

**18** [...] And as for me, a creature of dust, what [...] shall I say [...]

**19** [...] and what shall I devise for myself? For [...] in Your wrath [...]

**20** [...] Your wonderful [...] mysteries You have disclosed to the ear of dust [...]

**21** [...] and upon the heart of [...] You have inscribed eternal things [...]

**22** [...] and You have opened [...] the fountain of understanding [...]

**23** [...] for there is no [...] truth except from Your hand [...]

**24** [...] and no righteousness apart from Your counsel [...]

**25** [...] and all [...] are before You, and through the knowledge of [...]

**26** [...] Your truth You have established all things [...]

**27** [...] and without Your will nothing is accomplished [...]

**28** [...] and nothing is known apart from You [...]

**29** [...] Your wonderful mysteries [...] for eternity [...]

**30** [...] and ever [...]

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 26 is very fragmentary. The triple barukh ("Blessed are You") formula (26:3, 5) structures the surviving text as liturgical praise. The "ear of dust" (26:20) is a striking Hodayot expression for the human recipient of divine revelation — God whispers mysteries to creatures made from earth. Formal register maintained.*
